newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to publish Telefonica fees this week.
newsitem.headline: Spain to publish Telefonica fees this week.

text.p: Spain's Development Ministry said on Tuesday it would announce much-awaited fees for interconnection to Telefonica's networks this week.

Shares in the recently privatised telecoms operator were hit hard after press reports on Friday indicated that the interconnection fees its new competitor Retevision was to pay were substantially lower than those Telefonica had requested.
Telefonica de Espana shares recovered a bit on Tuesday, gaining 20 pesetas to 3,360 at midday, but were still down 4.9 percent since Friday.
Press reports had said the inter-provincial connection fee would be between 2.0 and 2.5 pesetas per minute in line with Retevision's proposal, but far from Telefonica's 7.0 pesetas.
Industry sources said the operator was pressuring the government to raise this tariff, one of the most important in its basic telephone service, to lessen the negative impact on its results.

"Yesterday there were rumours that the inter-provincial tariff could reach four pesetas per minute, but until there is an official declaration everything is pure speculation," an industry source told Reuters.

A ministry spokesman said the fee structure was already approved and just needed a little technical tinkering before being published. The ministry did not confirm whether the fees published in the press on Friday were correct.

"The Ministry will publish the interconnection fees this week. The economic affairs commission already knows what they are, but the Ministry still has to introduce some technical adjustments although they won't be substantial," he said.

Dealers said the fall in Telefonica shares was definitely due in part to the press reports on Friday because the lower connection fee would allow Retevision to offer cheaper long distance calls and could set off a price war.
Telefonica has 16.3 million lines in Spain from which it earned 1.4 trillion pesetas last year, not including earnings from international phone traffic.
